item.description:
作者：Amjad Masad 账号：@amasad 简介：ceo @replit. civilizationist
Honored to have the Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, help us open Replit’s first international office in London!
I’ve really appreciated the Mayor’s approach to AI, it feels very similar to ours. He calls himself an AI realist: clear-eyed about the disruption AI will create, but optimistic about the impact if we give people the tools and skills to participate in the coming revolution.
That’s exactly how we think about it at Replit. AI is going to transform work, so we have to make sure far more people can use it to create, build businesses, and access new opportunities.
It’s also why, as we establish ourselves here, we’re partnering with The Lord Mayor’s Appeal to help young Londoners from disadvantaged communities develop practical coding and AI skills.
London has the history, the talent, and the right leadership & philosophy for the AI era. We’re excited to be here.

item.description:
作者：Aaron Levie 账号：@levie 简介：ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
Good reminder here that with rapidly accelerating AI progress, you should likely be building with a vision that contemplates at least a few orders of magnitude of capability improvement or token volume available to you.
The best opportunities right now are those where you can value to customers today with things that are barely only possible, but with a full mission that feels nearly impossible with today’s tech.
There are lots of products the require orders of magnitude more processing of data (and thus are barely economically viable ideas) or where model capabilities still are in their infancy relative to what’s needed to work. Best to be building for those scenarios.

item.title: The AI jobs prediction so far is playing out the opposite of what many thought. The reason this is happening is because AI is bringing automation to areas that don’t have finite demand characteristics. AI allows companies to do far more than they could before, but agents still require human operato...
item.description:
作者：Aaron Levie 账号：@levie 简介：ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
The AI jobs prediction so far is playing out the opposite of what many thought.
The reason this is happening is because AI is bringing automation to areas that don’t have finite demand characteristics. AI allows companies to do far more than they could before, but agents still require human operators and oversight to generate value from them.
And not only has AI not replaced many of the types of jobs that theoretically would have been most affected by AI - engineers or lawyers - but AI is also creating or growing entire categories of jobs across the economy.
Cybersecurity, FDEs, agent operators, engineers in non-software domains, and tons of job categories are going to explode. It’s not clear if or when this trend will reverse because we keep discovering all new areas of demand that AI is going to open up.

item.title: A $10B Hedge Fund’s AI Playbook (Best of the Pod)
item.description:
播客：AI & I by Every
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:13 It's becoming a meme that CEOs are, like, writing basically, like, the We're AI first memo. You have the best example of that memo that I've ever seen. Would you mind just, like, reading, I don't know, maybe the first paragraph or two of what you wrote? Because I think it's amazing.
Speaker 2 | 00:13 - 00:29 Using ChatGPT is not cheating. That's a non applicable idea from academia. I use ChatGPT to write this email. You should be using it too and be proud of it. As a hedge fund, we should be ashamed to leave money on the table by ignoring tools that make us faster, smarter, and more effective.
Speaker 2 | 00:29 - 00:38 From the very top, we are building a culture around AI. Not using these tools is like refusing to use the Internet in 1995 because it wasn't perfect.
Speaker 1 | 00:52 - 00:53 Will, welcome to the show.
Speaker 2 | 00:53 - 00:55 Thanks, Ben. Thank you.
Speaker 1 | 00:55 - 01:24 So it's great to have you. For people who don't know you, you are the the benevolent dictator of Walleye, which is a close to 10,000,000,000 AUM hedge fund. And you're an every consulting client. We're working with you to help you do AI training and implementation inside of Walleye. And honestly, regardless of the stuff we've done, you're, I think, one of the most impressive examples of someone, a CEO, who is pivoting their entire organization around AI, and you're leading by example.
Speaker 1 | 01:24 - 01:25 And so I'm psyched to get to talk to you.
Speaker 2 | 01:25 - 01:41 Yeah. Thanks. Yeah. Maybe I could just give a little more context to that. I guess my my technical title is is CEO CIO managing partner, but, you know, both both the owner operator of, you know, one of the one of the larger hedge funds out there.
Speaker 2 | 01:41 - 01:50 I I don't do many press. You know, it's I don't typically speak at conferences. I've only done one other podcast. So this is very deliberate. It's very deliberate for me.
Speaker 2 | 01:51 - 02:37 And because of the relationship that we've developed on this subject, I do feel a great sense of both purpose and conviction about where our industry is going, where our firm is going. I do believe they're already a leader in that, and it's going to continue to be the case. So sometimes I listen to a lot of podcasts, so I was curious about some of the motivations for why people do this. I just want to be very clear upfront. Because I have that conviction, the skills to lead us into the next phase, and we'll get into that, of course, and ultimately the power to enact that, I really feel that it would be irresponsible of me not to go after it with sort of the maximum amount of discipline and intensity I can muster, which is a lot.
Speaker 2 | 02:37 - 03:12 So first, three main audiences here is the people at Walleye. We have about 400 people, not big for a normal company, but in our core of the world. That's not a small amount. Second, I'm also speaking to people that aren't at the firm today, but may join us in the future just to understand how serious the firm is about AI that ultimately starts with me and then others. And then third, finally speaking to people in the ecosystem, whether they be companies building products that firms like us can use or other ways of work together.
Speaker 2 | 03:14 - 03:21 That's why I'm here. But it does all start with me having, as I said, an enormous sense of conviction about where the world is heading.
Speaker 1 | 03:22 - 03:25 How did you develop that? What was that journey like for you? I actually don't even know this.
Speaker 2 | 03:25 - 03:48 So I'm a bonafide nerd by background. You know, I was an engineer at Princeton. I went to Oxford to do a PhD in math. I started my career writing code all day for algorithmic strategies. So we, as a firm, and me personally, have been using, let's just call it advanced statistics, even AI for years.
Speaker 2 | 03:48 - 04:19 A large part of what our firm does is in pure quant trading. So I've thought for many, many years about how machines increasingly can both either augment or do the jobs of humans and finance. That's nothing that's new for me. What has happened, of course, in recent years is just that a lot of these tools have become more powerful and they've also become more accessible to non technical people, particularly on unstructured data. And so part of it is just me personally, being curious, being interested.
Speaker 2 | 04:19 - 04:54 A huge part of this is about curiosity. Know, I've noticed the productivity improvements that I see using using these tools, just even for from a writing perspective, let alone some of the sort of more advanced things you can do. So it's a combination of called having been in deeply versed in technical background, as I said, bonafide nerd, and then noticing what's out there and just the sense of responsibility to the people at the firm, to our investors to say like, okay, we understand where this is going. If we ultimately get disrupted by AI, that's on me. And so let's get after that.
Speaker 2 | 04:54 - 05:24 So even two years ago, like this isn't a sense of, oh, yeah, we're going to do all these things in the future. You know, two years ago, we started an internal AI program, you know, today, you know, we're already doing a lot. So it's not just a story about what's to come. And yeah, a lot of that does start with me. Mean, a lot of times leader of organizations won't sort of say that how much actually matters, you know, that in the leadership, but this is one where I feel like I absolutely needed to lead from the front.
Speaker 1 | 05:24 - 05:45 Tell me about that, like a little bit more concretely, like one of the things I appreciate about you as a communicator is you're just kind of like no bullshit. We were talking, like, I don't know, three or four weeks ago, I was telling you something about every our strategy and direction. You were like, you sound kind of afraid. I was like, yeah. I'm a little afraid of this.
Speaker 1 | 05:45 - 06:05 So you're not you're not afraid to kinda, like, put your finger on the nerve, and you're also not particularly, like, hype y as a person, I don't think. So tell me about the moment where you're like, oh, we have to take this seriously versus it's just like it's just like, yeah, tech people, nerds are psyched about it, but it's something that we really need to understand.
Speaker 2 | 06:05 - 06:22 Yeah. And I appreciate you saying that. That's definitely the way I try to operate. Many people tell stories. Sometimes those stories get hyped and for whatever reason, I think a lot of it comes down to being comfortable with yourself, self confidence of not feeling like you need to convince something of someone you're not.

Speaker 1 | 06:26 - 06:30 Would never have done that. So I don't know from experience that that's a problem. Yeah.
